Coverage Indications, Limitations and/or Medical Necessity
Total knee arthroplasty is considered reasonable and necessary when all of the
following criteria are documented in the medical record.

The beneficiary has radiographic evidence of advanced degenerative joint disease
of the affected knee, demonstrated by joint space narrowing, subchondral
sclerosis, or osteophyte formation on imaging obtained within the preceding
twelve months.

The beneficiary reports functional impairment attributable to the affected knee
that limits activities of daily living, and this impairment is documented by the
treating practitioner using a validated functional assessment instrument.

The beneficiary has completed a trial of conservative therapy of at least twelve
weeks in duration within the preceding twelve months. Conservative therapy
includes supervised physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication where not
contraindicated, activity modification, or assistive device use.

Limitations
Total knee arthroplasty is not covered when the record documents active local or
systemic infection at the time of the proposed procedure, when the beneficiary has
a documented body mass index of 40 or greater without documented evaluation for
weight optimisation, or when the beneficiary remains an active tobacco user
without documented cessation counselling within the preceding six months.

Documentation Requirements
The medical record must contain the imaging report, the conservative therapy
record with dates and duration, and a validated functional assessment performed by
the treating practitioner.

Revision History
R4 effective 2023-07-01, superseding R3. Conservative therapy minimum duration
increased from six weeks to twelve weeks. Body mass index limitation threshold
reduced from 45 to 40. Functional assessment must now use a validated instrument.
